subproblem.title: Change of variables from ℝⁿ into WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) with normDet Jacobian (parent step 6)
subproblem.statement: Notation: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); n := m + k; P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) with its volume (the Lebesgue measure of the finite-dimensional inner product space P); Lⁿ = volume; normDet = LinearMap.normDet of the underlying linear map. Statement. Let m, k ∈ ℕ, f : ℝⁿ → P, f' : ℝⁿ → (ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] P) and B ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel, such that f has derivative f'(u) within B at every u ∈ B (HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' u) B u) and f is injective on B. Then for every function g : P → [0, ∞] (no measurability assumed): ∫_{f(B)} g d(volume) = ∫_B ofReal(normDet(f'(u)))·g(f(u)) dLⁿ(u).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ) (f : Rn (m + k) → WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k)) (f' : Rn (m + k) → Rn (m + k) →L[ℝ] WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k)) (B : Set (Rn (m + k))), MeasurableSet B → (∀ u ∈ B, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' u) B u) → InjOn f B → ∀ g : WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ w in f '' B, g w = ∫⁻ u in B, ENNReal.ofReal ((f' u).toLinearMap.normDet) * g (f u)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 6 (change of variables through a volume-preserving isometry P ≃ ℝⁿ).

1. finrank P = m + k: P ≃ₗ[ℝ] ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Rn m × Rn k), LinearEquiv.finrank_eq), Module.finrank_prod and finrank_euclideanSpace_fin. Also finrank ℝⁿ = m + k.

2. Choose a linear isometric equivalence e : P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝⁿ, namely e := ((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ P).reindex (finCongr h)).repr with h : finrank ℝ P = m + k from step 1 (its codomain EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (m + k)) is ℝⁿ). Write E : P →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ for e as a continuous linear map.

3. e⁻¹ is volume preserving (LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving: every linear isometric equivalence of finite-dimensional real inner product spaces preserves volume) and a measurable embedding (e.symm.toHomeomorph.measurableEmbedding). MeasurePreserving.setLIntegral_comp_emb for e⁻¹, the function g and the set e(f(B)) gives ∫_{e(f(B))} g(e⁻¹ v) dv = ∫_{e⁻¹(e(f(B)))} g dvol_P = ∫_{f(B)} g dvol_P (e⁻¹ ∘ e = id, Set.image_image).

4. Put f̂ := e ∘ f : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ. For u ∈ B, f̂ has derivative E ∘L f'(u) within B at u (chain rule: E.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivWithinAt). f̂ is injective on B because e is injective, and f̂(B) = e(f(B)) (Set.image_image).

5. Mathlib lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul (MeasureTheory/Function/Jacobian.lean), applied with the additive Haar measure volume on ℝⁿ, the Borel set B, the map f̂ with the derivatives of step 4 and the function v ↦ g(e⁻¹ v) (the lemma holds for every [0, ∞]-valued function), gives ∫_{f̂(B)} g(e⁻¹ v) dv = ∫_B ofReal|det(E ∘L f'(u))|·g(e⁻¹(e(f u))) du, and e⁻¹(e(f u)) = f(u).

6. For each u: det(E ∘L f'(u)) is the determinant of the linear endomorphism (E : P →ₗ ℝⁿ) ∘ₗ f'(u) of ℝⁿ (ContinuousLinearMap.det, ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap_comp), and |det| = normDet for endomorphisms (LinearMap.normDet_eq_abs_det). normDet((E) ∘ₗ f'(u)) = normDet(E)·normDet(f'(u)) (LinearMap.normDet_comp_of_finrank_eq, using finrank ℝⁿ = finrank P from step 1), and normDet(E) = 1 (LinearIsometry.normDet_eq_one applied to e.toLinearIsometry). Hence |det(E ∘L f'(u))| = normDet(f'(u)).

7. By steps 3, 4, 5 and 6 (setLIntegral_congr_fun on the Borel set B for the last rewriting), ∫_{f(B)} g dvol_P = ∫_{f̂(B)} g(e⁻¹ v) dv = ∫_B ofReal(normDet(f'(u)))·g(f u) du. ∎

subproblem.title: Slice integrals over a C¹ chart via the injective area formula (parent steps 1–3)
subproblem.statement: Notation: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); n := m + k; P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ), the Euclidean product, whose volume is the Lebesgue measure of the finite-dimensional inner product space P (instance measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace); toLp = WithLp.toLp 2; Hᵏ = μHE[k] (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Hausdorff outer measure); Lᵈ = volume; normDet = LinearMap.normDet, applied to the underlying linear map; DF(x) = fderiv ℝ F x (the zero map where F is not differentiable); j : ℝᵏ →L[ℝ] P is the continuous linear map z ↦ toLp(0, z), in Lean (WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (Rn m) (Rn k)).symm.toContinuousLinearMap.comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ (Rn m) (Rn k)) (j z = toLp(0, z) holds by rfl). For an open partial homeomorphism Φ from ℝⁿ to P: O := Φ.source and Ω := Φ.target (both open), Φ⁻¹ := Φ.symm, ρ := ψ ∘ Φ⁻¹ : P → ℝᴺ (in Lean ψ ∘ Φ.symm), h(w) := φ(ψ(Φ⁻¹ w))·ofReal(normDet(Dρ(w) ∘ j)) for w ∈ P, and F := 1_{Φ(B)}·h, i.e. F = (Φ '' B).indicator h. Statement. Let m, k, N ∈ ℕ and let Φ be an open partial homeomorphism from ℝⁿ to P such that Φ.symm is C¹ on Ω. Let ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ be C¹ on O and injective on O, and let G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ satisfy (Φ u).fst = G(u) for all u ∈ O. Let B ⊆ O be Borel and let φ : ℝᴺ → [0, ∞] be any function for which the injective area formula holds in dimension k: (AF) for every open V ⊆ ℝᵏ, every χ : ℝᵏ → ℝᴺ that is C¹ on V and injective on V, and every Borel S ⊆ V, ∫_{χ(S)} φ dHᵏ = ∫_S φ(χ(z))·ofReal(normDet(Dχ(z))) dLᵏ(z). Then for every y ∈ ℝᵐ: ∫_{ψ(B ∩ G⁻¹{y})} φ dHᵏ = ∫_{ℝᵏ} F(toLp(y, z)) dLᵏ(z). No measurability of φ and no differentiability of Φ is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m k N : ℕ) (ψ : Rn (m + k) → Rn N) (G : Rn (m + k) → Rn m) (Φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph (Rn (m + k)) (WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k))), ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ Φ.source → InjOn ψ Φ.source → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Φ.symm Φ.target → (∀ u ∈ Φ.source, (Φ u).fst = G u) → ∀ B ⊆ Φ.source, MeasurableSet B → ∀ φ : Rn N → ℝ≥0∞, (∀ (V : Set (Rn k)) (χ : Rn k → Rn N), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ V → InjOn χ V → ∀ S ⊆ V, MeasurableSet S → ∫⁻ x in χ '' S, φ x ∂μHE[k] = ∫⁻ z in S, φ (χ z) * ENNReal.ofReal ((fderiv ℝ χ z).toLinearMap.normDet)) → ∀ y : Rn m, ∫⁻ x in ψ '' (B ∩ G ⁻¹' {y}), φ x ∂μHE[k] = ∫⁻ z : Rn k, (Φ '' B).indicator (fun w ↦ φ (ψ (Φ.symm w)) * ENNReal.ofReal (((fderiv ℝ (ψ ∘ Φ.symm) w).comp ((WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (Rn m) (Rn k)).symm.toContinuousLinearMap.comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ (Rn m) (Rn k)))).toLinearMap.normDet)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (y, z))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1–3 (slices of the chart and the area formula on every slice). Hypothesis (AF) is exactly the conclusion of the sibling c1_injective_area (Submission.pcoarea_c1_injOn_area_formula) for the fixed k, N, φ; the parent discharges it with that sibling.

Standing facts about Φ (OpenPartialHomeomorph API): O and Ω are open (Φ.open_source, Φ.open_target); Φ maps O into Ω (Φ.map_source) and Φ⁻¹ maps Ω into O (Φ.map_target); Φ⁻¹(Φ u) = u for u ∈ O (Φ.left_inv); Φ is continuous and injective on O (Φ.continuousOn, Φ.injOn); Φ⁻¹ is injective on Ω (Φ.symm.injOn, as Φ.symm.source = Ω).

Fix y ∈ ℝᵐ. Put B' := Φ(B), ι(z) := toLp(y, z) for z ∈ ℝᵏ, V := ι⁻¹(Ω), S := ι⁻¹(B') and χ(z) := ψ(Φ⁻¹(ι z)).

1. The slice map ι. ι = (WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ ℝᵐ ℝᵏ).symm ∘ (z ↦ (y, z)). The inner map has derivative ContinuousLinearMap.inr at every point (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_right) and the outer map is a continuous linear equivalence, so by the chain rule HasFDerivAt ι j z for every z; equivalently ι(z) = toLp(y, 0) + j(z) is affine. ι is C¹ (ContinuousLinearEquiv.contDiff composed with contDiff_const.prodMk contDiff_id), hence continuous, and injective, because the second component of ι(z) is z (apply WithLp.snd).

2. B' is a Borel subset of Ω. B ⊆ O and Φ is continuous and injective on O, hence on B; ℝⁿ is Polish and P carries its Borel σ-algebra (WithLp.borelSpace), so the Lusin–Souslin theorem MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn gives MeasurableSet B'. Every point of B' is Φ(u) with u ∈ B ⊆ O, so B' ⊆ Ω.

3. V is open (Ω open, ι continuous: IsOpen.preimage), S is Borel (ι is measurable and B' is Borel), and S ⊆ V (because B' ⊆ Ω).

4. χ is C¹ on V: ι is C¹ and maps V into Ω by definition of V; Φ⁻¹ is C¹ on Ω and maps Ω into O; ψ is C¹ on O. Two applications of ContDiffOn.comp give ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ V.

5. χ is injective on V. Let z₁, z₂ ∈ V with χ(z₁) = χ(z₂). Then Φ⁻¹(ι z₁), Φ⁻¹(ι z₂) ∈ O, so injectivity of ψ on O gives Φ⁻¹(ι z₁) = Φ⁻¹(ι z₂); injectivity of Φ⁻¹ on Ω (ι z₁, ι z₂ ∈ Ω) gives ι(z₁) = ι(z₂); injectivity of ι gives z₁ = z₂.

6. ψ(B ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = χ(S).
(⊆) Let u ∈ B with G(u) = y. Since u ∈ O, (Φ u).fst = G(u) = y, so ι((Φ u).snd) = toLp((Φ u).fst, (Φ u).snd) = Φ(u) (this holds definitionally: (Φ u).fst and (Φ u).snd are the components of ofLp(Φ u), and toLp ∘ ofLp = id). Hence z := (Φ u).snd satisfies ι(z) = Φ(u) ∈ B', i.e. z ∈ S, and χ(z) = ψ(Φ⁻¹(Φ u)) = ψ(u).
(⊇) Let z ∈ S. Then ι(z) ∈ B', so Φ(u) = ι(z) for some u ∈ B. As u ∈ O, G(u) = (Φ u).fst = (ι z).fst = y, so u ∈ B ∩ G⁻¹{y}; and ψ(u) = ψ(Φ⁻¹(Φ u)) = ψ(Φ⁻¹(ι z)) = χ(z).

7. Area formula on the slice. By steps 3–5, (AF) applies to V, χ and S: ∫_{χ(S)} φ dHᵏ = ∫_S φ(χ z)·ofReal(normDet(Dχ(z))) dz. By step 6 the left-hand side equals ∫_{ψ(B ∩ G⁻¹{y})} φ dHᵏ.

8. Derivative on the slice. Let z ∈ V. Φ⁻¹ is C¹ on the open set Ω ∋ ι(z), hence differentiable at ι(z) (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≠ 0, then DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt with IsOpen.mem_nhds); likewise ψ is differentiable at Φ⁻¹(ι z) ∈ O. So ρ = ψ ∘ Φ⁻¹ is differentiable at ι(z) (DifferentiableAt.comp). Since χ = ρ ∘ ι, the chain rule fderiv_comp and step 1 (HasFDerivAt.fderiv) give Dχ(z) = Dρ(ι z) ∘L j.

9. Pointwise identity. For z ∈ S: χ(z) = ψ(Φ⁻¹(ι z)) and, by step 8 (S ⊆ V), Dχ(z) = Dρ(ι z) ∘L j, so φ(χ z)·ofReal(normDet(Dχ z)) = h(ι z) = F(ι z), because ι(z) ∈ B'. For z ∉ S: ι(z) ∉ B', so F(ι z) = 0. Hence 1_S(z)·φ(χ z)·ofReal(normDet(Dχ z)) = F(toLp(y, z)) for every z ∈ ℝᵏ (Set.indicator_of_mem, Set.indicator_of_notMem).

10. Conclusion. ∫_S φ(χ z)·ofReal(normDet(Dχ(z))) dz = ∫_{ℝᵏ} 1_S(z)·φ(χ z)·ofReal(normDet(Dχ z)) dz (lintegral_indicator, S Borel) = ∫_{ℝᵏ} F(toLp(y, z)) dz (lintegral_congr and step 9). Together with step 7 this proves the claim. No measurability of φ is used. ∎
